question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed Claw package, manifest, ownership, publication, and lifecycle contract as RFC 0016?
rationale: The patch is coherent and well-evidenced, but it creates a new cross-repository product surface whose long-term compatibility and ownership commitments require explicit human acceptance under the repository's RFC process.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Confirm the current product and compatibility boundaries, create the implementation issue, update the RFC metadata to accepted, and merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Defer selected update, export, MCP, cron, publication, or shared-package semantics before accepting a smaller v1 surface.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC open as draft while experimental implementation experience resolves remaining product choices.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the current product and compatibility boundaries, create the implementation issue, update the RFC metadata to accepted, and merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the most substantive visible product-model review and their requested boundaries now define the proposal's central contract.
